rationale: R names a dependency FOUR ways and every one of them lands on this file. `library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)` and `require(methods, character.only = TRUE)` attach a PACKAGE and sit at 0.8, because `warn.conflicts` / `character.only` are named arguments that a positional reader would mistake for the package name -- the confidence is the attribution's and this fixture is why it is below 1.0. `library("stats")` is the same package named by a STRING and is 1.0: there is no second reading of it. `source("helpers.R")` and `sourceCpp("code.cpp")` name a FILE ON DISK, which is a dependency whatever the grammar calls it and which a grammar inventory cannot see because it is a string -- the same reason json's `imports` ruling needed instrument B. `dplyr::filter` and `internal:::secret()` reach a package through `::` and `:::`, and the TARGET is the PACKAGE (`dplyr`, `internal`), never the function: `imports global -> filter` is forbidden because it would assert a package called `filter` exists. The file has NO symbols at all, which is the point -- a dependency is not a declaration.
